headline_marked: Bangladesh signs [[15-year deal with DP World]] to operate Ctg port's NCT
headline: Bangladesh signs 15-year deal with DP World to operate Ctg port's NCT
summary: The Dubai-based company will invest over 1,000 crore BDT in modernization, while the port authority retains ownership and control of the land and infrastructure.
details: The Chittagong Port Authority has signed a 15-year agreement with Dubai-based DP World to operate and manage the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT). The deal was signed on Thursday in Dhaka.

Shipping Minister Sheikh Rabiul Alam stated that the ownership, land, and infrastructure of the NCT will remain with the Chittagong Port Authority. DP World has committed to an upfront fee of approximately 600 crore BDT and over 1,000 crore BDT in investment for modernization, equipment, and technology over the first 10 years.

Under the financial terms, the Chittagong Port Authority will receive a share of the revenue and a fixed annual fee. DP World will provide 67% of the earnings from each TEU container handling to the port authority, estimated at 93 to 103 USD per container.

DP World's Executive Chairman Esa Kazim stated that the partnership will connect the NCT to DP World's global logistics and supply chain network, enhancing Bangladesh's commercial links with international markets.

The New Mooring Container Terminal is a critical asset, currently handling approximately 44% of Chittagong Port's total container handling. It has been managed by Chittagong Dry Dock Limited since July 2025.
The agreement was signed amid protests from leftist groups and the 'Port Protection Committee,' who oppose the deal. Police baton-charged protesters to disperse them during the demonstrations.
caption:
A 15-year deal has been signed for Dubai's DP World to operate the New Mooring Container Terminal in Chittagong.

The Chittagong Port Authority has signed a 15-year agreement with Dubai-based DP World to operate and manage the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT). The deal was signed on Thursday in Dhaka.

Shipping Minister Sheikh Rabiul Alam stated that the ownership, land, and infrastructure of the NCT will remain with the Chittagong Port Authority. DP World has committed to an upfront fee of approximately 600 crore BDT and over 1,000 crore BDT in investment for modernization, equipment, and technology over the first 10 years.

Under the financial terms, the Chittagong Port Authority will receive a share of the revenue and a fixed annual fee. DP World will provide 67% of the earnings from each TEU container handling to the port authority, estimated at 93 to 103 USD per container.

DP World's Executive Chairman Esa Kazim stated that the partnership will connect the NCT to DP World's global logistics and supply chain network, enhancing Bangladesh's commercial links with international markets.

The New Mooring Container Terminal is a critical asset, currently handling approximately 44% of Chittagong Port's total container handling. It has been managed by Chittagong Dry Dock Limited since July 2025.

The agreement was signed amid protests from leftist groups and the 'Port Protection Committee,' who oppose the deal. Police baton-charged protesters to disperse them during the demonstrations.

headline_marked: 5 deaths in 24 hours: [[Dengue claims 5 more lives]] in Bangladesh
headline: 5 deaths in 24 hours: Dengue claims 5 more lives in Bangladesh
summary: Nearly 2,000 people were hospitalized within a single day as the death toll for the year reaches 294, according to the DGHS.
details: Five people died from dengue in the last 24 hours, according to a notice from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) issued on Thursday.
In the same period, 1,935 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country.
The total number of dengue deaths this year has now reached 294.
Since the beginning of the year, a total of 94,151 people have been hospitalized due to dengue.
Of those, 88,208 patients have been discharged from the hospital.
caption:
5 deaths in 24 hours and nearly 2,000 new hospitalizations. Dengue continues to surge across Bangladesh.

Five people died from dengue in the last 24 hours, according to a notice from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) issued on Thursday.

In the same period, 1,935 new patients were admitted to hospitals across the country.

The total number of dengue deaths this year has now reached 294.

Since the beginning of the year, a total of 94,151 people have been hospitalized due to dengue.

Of those, 88,208 patients have been discharged from the hospital.
